newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real drops 0.02 pct on lower mini-band.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real drops 0.02 pct on lower mini-band.

text.p: Brazil's real fell 0.02 percent to close at 1.0861 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market after the Central Bank lowered the reais-dollar mini-band, dealers said.
The Central Bank reduced the mini-band Thursday for the third time this month, lowering it 0.09 percent to between 1.0860 and 1.0910 reais per dollar through a buy/sell auction.

The previous mini-band was set Aug 7 at between 1.0850 and 1.0900 per dollar. So far this month, the mini-band has fallen 0.28 percent against the dollar compared to monthly declines of between 0.57 and 0.61 percent in the past six months.
The real was supported by banks that had been holding dollars over the last few days awaiting the mini-band drop, dealers said.
The Central Bank bought dollars at 1.0860 per greenback to drain excess dollars from the market in the late afternoon.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real closed at 1.0915 per dollar, down 0.04 percent.
In the parallel market, the real rose 0.18 percent to end at 1.138 reais per greenback.
